title: Benchmarking semantic code retrieval on Claude Code — Kuba Rogut, Turbopuffer
talk_summary: Speaker benchmarks semantic code retrieval as an extra tool in Claude Code against grep and windowed grep using a ContextBench-style file/line/symbol retrieval eval. Semantic search raised file precision and helped find behavior-adjacent files, but did not improve recall overall and depended on task type and the agent knowing when to call it.

takeaways.technique: Semantic code index as cached retrieval tool
takeaways.what_they_do: They chunk code with tree-splitter, embed with Voyage code model, upload to Turbopuffer, and expose a search tool to Claude Code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: chunk it, embed it using the Voyage code model and then upload it to Turbo Puffer
takeaways.numbers: File precision 65% baseline to 87% with windowed grep + semantic; wasted file reads 1 in 3 to 1 in 8.

takeaways.what_they_do: They cap reads to 50 lines at a time so agents inspect targeted ranges instead of whole large files.
takeaways.evidence_quote: max of 50 line reads at a time
takeaways.numbers: Baseline file precision 65%, line precision 33%, symbol precision 43%; windowed grep improved precision.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid grep plus semantic search by task type
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep keyword grep for import tracing and add semantic search for behavior-adjacent files that lack shared keywords.
takeaways.evidence_quote: certain tasks requires different types of tools
takeaways.numbers: Semantic search did not improve overall recall; task-level split showed semantic wins on behavior-adjacent files and grep wins on import tracing.

takeaways.technique: Explicit tool-routing skills for extra retrieval tools
takeaways.what_they_do: They note Claude Code is built for grep, so an added semantic tool was not reliably called at the right time; Cursor's built-in integration saw larger gains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's very hard for it to have a true understanding of when to use it
takeaways.numbers: Cursor cited 24% relative answer accuracy improvement, 12.5-13% across models, 2.6% code retention, 2.2% fewer dissatisfied requests.

takeaways.what_they_do: They observe semantic retrieval works best with inline comments; Cursor reportedly injects comments before embedding code chunks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: works best when there's a lot of like comments on code

takeaways.what_they_do: They use human-labeled tasks to test whether the agent found the right files, lines, and symbols, not just whether it solved the task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: did it find certain files? Did it find certain lines and it find certain symbols?
takeaways.numbers: 50 tasks; measured file/line/symbol precision and recall.
